t.E102.agn: In its 2009 re-evaluation EFSA maintained the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 7.5 mg/kg body weight. It stated that intolerance reactions may occur in a small number of people even at amounts below this limit. In the EU, the labels of products containing this colour must carry a warning that it may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children.
t.E102.body: In humans and laboratory animals, typically less than 5% of orally ingested tartrazine is absorbed; the absorbed part is mainly excreted unchanged in the urine. The unabsorbed part is broken down by reduction by gut bacteria; small amounts of the resulting products, such as sulphanilic acid, are absorbed and excreted in the urine.
t.E102.eff.0.t: May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children; in the EU this warning is mandatory on the label of products containing it. EFSA did not confirm a causal link with individual colours
t.E102.eff.1.a: Even at amounts below the daily limit
t.E102.eff.1.w: A small number of sensitive people
t.E102.eval: In the EU, the labels of products containing this colour must carry the warning “may have an adverse effect on attention and activity in children” (following the 2007 Southampton study). In the US it is permitted under the name “Yellow 5”.
t.E102.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis.
